- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast; increase forecast slightly to align with sentiment momentum.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.5) and prices are trending down, model often over-anticipates recovery; reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overshoot.  
- Model consistently under-forecasts in the 10–15 day horizon after a sharp price spike; add 2–5% to forecast for that window to account for lag.  
- If sentiment swings sharply upward after a downtrend, model often fails to capture the reversal; adjust forecast upward by 3–7% in the next 5–7 days.  
- Model shows persistent mean reversion bias: if forecast is 5% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% to avoid overbought signal.  
- In 30-day horizon, model frequently underestimates final price by 2–5% when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive; add 1–3% to forecast to compensate.
